narrative:
Based on the information provided, the model estimates that you have a 22% chance of not passing your final year. Because this is above the school’s threshold of 10%, you are required to take additional remedial courses to support your learning and help ensure your success.

The model’s decision was influenced most strongly by three aspects of your profile. First, your record shows that you have not failed any classes in the past, which is a positive sign and actually reduced your risk compared to others. Most students in your situation also have no previous failures, so this is in line with your peers and worked in your favor.

However, the fact that you are currently taking extra paid classes within your course subject set you apart from most students—only about 3% of students in your group do this. The model interpreted this as a sign that you might be struggling with the material, which increased your predicted risk of failing.

Finally, your strong desire to pursue higher education helped lower your risk. Every student in your group shares this goal, and it is generally associated with greater motivation and better outcomes.

Given these factors, the requirement to take remedial courses is not a judgment of your abilities, but rather a precaution to give you extra support. You should take advantage of these courses to strengthen your understanding and address any challenges early. If you have concerns or feel you need different support, consider discussing your situation with your teachers or school counselor.
